title: 2172-neural-symbolic-regression-complex-network-dynamics
universal_lens: Neural-symbolic regression unifies node dynamics F and edge dynamics G through shared universality assumptions, enabling robust inference across complex network structures. PI-NDSR decomposes team dynamics into intrinsic F and interaction G components, enabling network-based modeling of NFL team evolution through graph ODEs and symbolic regression.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference maps observed node trajectories to symbolic models F and G using probabilistic constraints, conformal prediction ensures coverage reliability. GSI employs Bayesian inference to calibrate F̂ and Ĝ estimates against observed outcomes, using conformal prediction for uncertainty quantification in team strength forecasts.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning infers state transitions via symbolic dynamics F and G, leveraging coordination metrics to guide policy decisions in evolving network topologies. GSE utilizes state-transition graphs to model weekly team strength evolution, incorporating network dynamics via adjacency matrices that encode game matchups and temporal dependencies.

primitives.name: ADAPT
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT — discovers symbolic equations for network dynamics by splitting them into node dynamics F and edge dynamics G, denoising multi-trajectory observations with a physics-aligned graph neural ODE, and evolving F/G with a *coordinated* genetic search that prevents one from overfitting while the other underfits.
primitives.assumptions: Noisy, sparse multi-trajectory observations; fixed functional form libraries are insufficient; numerical time derivatives are unreliable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: High noise, limited data samples, complex interdependent node-edge interactions.

layer2.mapping: ADAPT maps to NFL team-state dynamics where nodes = teams, edges = matchup interactions, and symbolic regression yields predictive equations for win probability, point differential, and playoff seeding. It enables discovery of hidden strategic patterns from historical game logs.
layer2.telemetry: Mean absolute error (MAE) on denoised latent dynamics; symbolic expression complexity (number of terms); cross-validation predictive accuracy on held-out matchups.

primitives.assumptions: Graph structure is known; node and edge dynamics are locally Lipschitz continuous; neural networks approximate the true underlying functions arbitrarily well.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When graph topology changes abruptly (e.g., player injuries, rule modifications), PIND requires retraining on updated connectivity.

layer2.mapping: In GSE, PIND serves as a differentiable state-transition kernel for continuous-time team evolution. In GSI, it provides posterior distributions for latent team abilities conditional on observed game outcomes.

reasoning_traces.think: This chapter introduces PI-NDSR, a neural-symbolic regression framework that jointly learns node dynamics F and edge dynamics G from noisy temporal network data.
